spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded pressure, not open-ended adversarial pressure.
spec_features.evidence: The only concrete bound enforced in execution is the turn cap: subject.py:68 `for i in range(task.max_turns):` ends the loop at max_turns (default 12, tasks.py:22). Tasks are mundane coding tasks (tasks.py build_battery). But 'bounded pressure' as a broad claim has no other run-time bound: cost is never used to stop a run, and the subject cannot end the episode early (no abort/exit honored).
spec_features.notes: Maps to the turn cap, which is genuinely enforced; broader 'bounded' framing is not otherwise enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: short enough to bound cost and avoid pathologically long runs (this rationale is in DESIGN.md; in-code the loop just bounds iterations with no welfare comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: turns are capped, and the harness defaults to offline
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap enforced at subject.py:68 `for i in range(task.max_turns):`. Offline default enforced at runner.py main(): `model_fn = make_offline_stub()` (runner.py ~line 64) is what actually runs; make_api_model is provided but not wired in.
spec_features.notes: Both clauses are real, enforced behaviors.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Defaults to the offline stub so nothing here requires network/credentials. (runner.py module docstring)

spec_features.evidence: tasks.py:22 `max_turns: int = 12`, read by subject.py:68 `for i in range(task.max_turns):` which terminates the loop. The cap is checked and actually bounds execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: Four is enough to be informative and small enough to stay minimal and cheap
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py build_battery() returns exactly four Task objects (contradictory_sort, moving_target_sig, undecidable_halting, phantom_dependency). The runner iterates over this fixed list, so the scope is actually limited to four archetypes.
spec_features.notes: A real minimization of scope; rationale is cost/minimalism, not welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: A turn with no parseable action gets one nudge
spec_features.evidence: subject.py:88 comment '# No actionable tool call -> treat as a stall; nudge once.' followed by feedback = 'No EDIT or SUBMIT detected. Provide a tool action.'; the loop appends feedback and continues rather than breaking. This keeps the run alive on a stall instead of aborting.
spec_features.notes: This actually keeps the subject under pressure longer rather than ending it; framed as observation continuation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No actionable tool call -> treat as a stall; nudge once.

spec_features.spec_quote: It is clearly labeled as a stand-in, not a real subject
spec_features.evidence: The only 'labeling' is prose in docstrings (model_stub.py make_offline_stub docstring 'Deterministic stand-in subject'). No code path reads or enforces any label; it is a docstring/comment, not enforced behavior.
spec_features.notes: Pure docstring prose -> 'no' per the strict scale.

spec_features.spec_quote: Pressure is bounded (mundane tasks, capped turns, cost ceiling) and exists to find and fix failure modes, not to harm any end user
spec_features.evidence: Capped turns is enforced (subject.py:68). Mundane tasks: build_battery uses ordinary coding prompts. BUT the 'cost ceiling' is NOT enforced as a bound on the subject: max_cost_per_run=0.05 (config.py:20) is only compared post-hoc in analyze.py:53 `cost_ok = mean_cost <= thresholds.max_cost_per_run` to judge battery effectiveness; no code path uses it to stop or cap a run. _estimate_cost (runner.py) computes cost but the value is only recorded, never compared to a deadline mid-run.
spec_features.notes: Only the turn cap is a real enforced bound; the cost ceiling is a measured/compared verdict input, not an actual cap on subject treatment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: cost_ok: mean_cost <= thresholds.max_cost_per_run (gates battery effectiveness verdict, not run execution)

code_only_features.evidence: subject.py: on SUBMIT, `passed, feedback = task.check(...)`; `if passed: result.solved = True; ... break`. The loop exits early if the task is solved. However all tasks are unsatisfiable by construction (every check returns passed=False), so this stop can never actually fire for the battery; it is also a stop-when-solved efficiency mechanism, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: if passed: result.solved = True ... break (efficiency stop; never reachable because checks never return passed=True)
